response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: Fishing. Though so far, I've only caught things that aren't fish.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: If it were knick-knacks from shipwrecks, that'd be fine, 'cause traveling merchants would buy those. I once pulled up a boot with half a... *sigh* Forget it. Talking about stuff like that will scare the fish off.

choices.text: Is there anything of note nearby?

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: Treasure hunting again, huh? That "Great Treasure" they say lies east of the moon and west of the sun... Doesn't take much to know this isn't the place to find it.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: There've been a good few shipwrecks in these waters. There may well be treasure beneath the waves, not that you'd find it easy to get at.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: I heard talk at the tavern, too, from sailors who escaped their sinking ship. Said it happened on a moonless night, yet something was glowing among the towering waves.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: They swore it was one-eyed Kratti, a monster that could swallow the moon. It was fighting a giant sea serpent for the right to rule its territory.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: For a long time after that, this whole stretch of ocean stayed as dark as ink. No ships dared pass through — they all feared the lost souls beneath the waves would drag them down.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: Whether those souls still linger on... Who knows for sure? Either way, I can't see 'em.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: It's cursed. There used to be a whirlpool here — the sailors called it the Eye of Kratti. Then one day, this tree just started growing right out of it.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: And that wasn't the only strange thing that happened around that time. Tracing it back, it all started with those rocks falling from the sky... Who knows? Maybe this tree's from the same place.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: Then there are those little shiny things that appear every now and then, rare as you like, those are. I figured there might be new kinds of fish, too. That's why I came out here — to try my luck.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: I used to have a fishing buddy who came out here, too, but he said he kept hearing strange singing. It spooked him so bad, he never came back. Hah, only half a Frostmoon Scion that one, but he inherited every one of their odd little habits.

choices.text: About the Proofs of the Cognoscenti...

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: The "Proofs of the Cognoscenti," the "Great Treasure that lies east of the moon and west of the sun"... If you ask me...

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: Folks who greedily chase what isn't theirs rarely come to a good end. Take the Atlas, for example — I heard Captain Grettir was bewitched by all that talk of treasure.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: In the end, he met his fate at the bottom of the sea. And the treasure? It's not like it stayed buried with him. All that fuss for nothing.

response.speaker: Ilmari
response.text: No worries. There's not a single fish in sight anyway.
